I've been playing Civilization since it first started. I worked at Software Etc and purchased Civilization on release in 91. Have been chasing "one more turn" ever since and have every single Civ game ever released, including my original boxed Civilization. I believe Civ, as a series, is the greatest game of all time. No other game series has commanded more of my time. None.

However.....Civ VI is just not good. There are myriad reasons, but it just isn't. Too many bugs. AI is GOD AWFUL. Trying to find the right combination of DLC, mods and what-have-you to get it working sort of, is just too much.

Quite simply, this game just isn't very good.

To be honest, I prefer Civ 6 over Civ 5 for a few reasons such as better graphics, more dynamic gameplay and mechanics. The separation of Tech tree and Civic tree, the decluttering of districts, buildings and wonders from your cities, as well as Eurekas and Inspiration boost are well served for role-playing. In Gathering Storm expansion, what I really enjoy, the new natural disaster and climate change spice up the game quite a lot. The addition of Favor system copied from Beyond Earth is also welcome. The AIs, in the other hand, are just as bad as Civ 5, notoriously in term of trading.

I do believe that with the latest expansion, Civ 6 has already surpassed Civ 5 to be the best game on my PC right now.
Having played CIV 5 and Now 6, I will say the game has its points but misses in some areas, is the best for those who are new to 4x games as a genre

Its another Civ game, updated graphics and minor tweaks to the rules. Much easier to live a peaceful existence with the war penalties, and the game does a bit better of a job explaining some of the in depth features. There are still some things like the national parks that require third party research. 10/10 will play more than once!

Holy shit hell yes! I was really doubtful about the district mechanics when switching from Civ 5 to Civ 6, but there are so many changes to gameplay mechanics and tons of quality of life improvements that I now finally understand the reviewer hype for the game.

Since I really only just got into Civ 6, I can't speak to previous pricing schemes for the base game and the DLC - I was able to buy the bundle pack for a pretty decent price (like $20? I don't remember). So I can understand if the game was previously overpriced, but right now I'd say I got my money's worth. I'd recommend getting a DLC bundle that includes, at minimum, Gathering Storm and Rise and Fall - though I am biased towards the Australia civ pack as well for personal reasons.

Perfect chill yet complex game. Fun strategy math puzzle hidden beneath the great stylized flavor of history and politics. For players new to the 4X grand strategy genre, as is true with many of them, it takes a few hours of helpful tutorials to learn the basics, probably 20 hours to begin getting comfortable with intermediate features, 100 hours to play on some of the harder difficulties or learn more advanced strategies. I enjoy it more than Civ 5 and other 4X titles, but I am biased since I began with 6.

You start the game, meet the Romans, its the year -4000. Boom, they'll condemn you for not having alot of cities while you both just founded your first. Have less ships then Norway? You'll never be their allies. Have 1 more wonder then the Chinese? They'll hate you forever. The AI in this game is so annoyingly childish that you'll end up most games wanting to destroy everyone. At first, I was very skeptical of the graphics. Everything looked very "cartoonish." Once I started playing, however, I immediately fell in love. The graphics actually make the game very playable by not taking too much processing power. Sometimes 5 and even Beyond Earth became too frustrating to play those larger games with more computer/human players. The Civ team was very smart in not putting too much effort into the graphics by making sure this is playable on most hardware, even making it simple enough to easily put it on a mobile platform.

As for game mechanics, this version introduces a lot and re-introduces what we love about previous versions. New to the franchise, they brought districts to the map, limited actions for builders, policy card decks, envoys, super enhanced diplomacy, and culture "researching." Then they made sure to include features that I love about previous versions like religion, choosing government, rebels, trade, and natural wonders. This makes the base game already feel really complete. It's hard to imagine what they might include in the expansions, other than new civs and maps. Or maybe I'm just blindsighted at how awesome the game already is.

For long time Civilization players, this is the game we've always wanted.
